qt: to the Commission Magdalena Adamowicz (PPE) Subject:

In recital 36 of the draft EU KIDS Act – a regulation aimed at protecting children online – the Commission acknowledges that open chat rooms in online games expose minors to contact with individuals who seek to groom them, sexually exploit them, recruit them into gangs, or draw them into violence, radicalisation and terrorism. Europol warns that gangs are recruiting teenagers to carry out acts of violence on their behalf via chat rooms on gaming platforms and instant messaging services. According to Member States’ intelligence services, foreign states are commissioning minors to carry out acts of sabotage. Article 12(2) requires social media sites and video platforms to protect minors from being persuaded to consent to contact, as this forms the basis for grooming and recruitment. Article 15 expands Article 12(1) – the prohibition on contacting a child without their consent – to in-game chat rooms, but omits Article 12(2). Furthermore, it protects minors from being lured out of chat rooms into out-ofgame contact, but not from being directed to illegal content. 1.
Will the Commission support expanding the obligation under Article 12(2) to cover ingame chats?
Does the prohibition under Article 12(1) cover text and voice chats with players randomly assigned to play together?
Will the Commission support expand Article 15(2) to cover the directing of minors via online game chats towards illegal content?
